reason: Combining hydrogen nuclei with electrons should begin forming neutral gas and help free the trapped light.
expectation: I expect neutral hydrogen to form, potentially letting radiation travel more freely; the light may require another step.

alternatives.reason: Helium can also capture electrons, but I chose hydrogen first.

effect: Neutral hydrogen has formed; helium is the only available combination.
reaction: The distinction between making an atom and making an element was useful.
reason: I'll combine helium nuclei with electrons because it is the only offered gameplay action.
expectation: I expect helium atoms to form, though I don't know whether this will immediately free the light.

effect: Neutral helium has formed, leaving the two neutral gases available to combine.
reaction: The clarification that the icon represents the full recombination process was useful.
reason: I'll combine the neutral gases because it is the only offered gameplay action and may gather the first star-making gas.
expectation: I expect a mixture of neutral hydrogen and helium, though I don't know whether it will complete a goal.

effect: The neutral gases form primordial gas, which can now be used to free radiation or gather in a denser region.
reaction: The absence of rock and water clarifies how early this stage is.
reason: I'll combine the primordial gas with trapped radiation to pursue the goal of letting light travel.
expectation: I expect the neutral gas to allow radiation to travel freely, though another step may be needed.

alternatives.reason: The denser patch may gather star-making gas, but I'll pursue the light first.

effect: The light is free to travel, completing that goal; the denser patch remains available for gathering gas.
reaction: The link between fewer free electrons and transparency was clear.
reason: I'll use the denser patch to pursue the remaining goal of gathering star-making gas.
expectation: I expect primordial gas to accumulate in the denser region, perhaps forming a gas cloud.

alternatives.reason: Expanding space may change the travelling light, but gathering gas addresses the remaining goal.

effect: Gravity has gathered gas in a denser region, but the star-making gas goal remains open.
reaction: The distinction between cosmic expansion and bound regions was useful.
reason: I'll add neutral hydrogen to the gathering gas to pursue the remaining goal.
expectation: I expect a denser hydrogen-rich gas cloud, possibly completing the goal.

alternatives.reason: Expansion may change the travelling light, but the gas combination seems more directly tied to the remaining goal.

effect: The dense gas knot completes the remaining goal and establishes that cooling is needed before it can contract into a star.
reaction: The cooling condition made the outcome more interesting than simply gathering enough gas.

mostWorthwhile.text: Freeing the light was most worthwhile: it clearly connected neutral atoms, reduced scattering and a transparent universe.

leastWorthwhile.text: Combining the two neutral gases felt relatively routine, though the description of primordial gas provided useful context.

surprise.text: I was struck that bound regions can gather under gravity while expansion continues elsewhere.

arbitrary.text: Adding neutral hydrogen to gas already described as primordial felt somewhat mechanically arbitrary, although the result explained it as hydrogen flowing into the growing knot.

continue.text: Yes. The need for the gas to lose heat before making a star gives me a concrete reason to see what happens next.
